package_info.why_malicious: The package and its many typosquat variants are designed to masquerade as popular libraries (react, angular) and execute code at install time to exfiltrate host information to an external Discord webhook. This is a clear violation of user trust and constitutes data exfiltration malware.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation (preinstall), the package executes a Node.js script (new.js), enabling arbitrary code execution before the package is fully installed.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Preinstall scripts are a common vector for supply chain attacks, as they allow code to run automatically on user systems without explicit consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely require preinstall scripts, especially for libraries. Running arbitrary code at install time is not expected.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages use preinstall for build steps or environment checks, but not for exfiltrating data.
key_indicators: Execution of external file (new.js) during install

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install time (preinstall), the code collects all network interface addresses and the hostname, then sends this information via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded Discord webhook, enabling host data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects sensitive host information and exfiltrates it to an external service (Discord webhook) without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package install scripts do not collect or transmit host/network information. This is a clear violation of privacy and security expectations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, telemetry or error reporting might collect environment info, but always with user consent and never to a Discord webhook.
key_indicators: Use of os.networkInterfaces() and os.hostname() to gather host data
HTTPS POST of collected data during install

attack_chain.action: User installs a typosquat package (e.g., zngularjs) believing it to be a legitimate library.
The preinstall script defined in package.json triggers execution of new.js.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code in new.js

attack_chain.action: new.js collects network interface addresses and hostname, then sends this data to a Discord webhook via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of host data to attacker

behavioral_signatures: Execution of preinstall scripts that invoke external JavaScript files
Collection of network interface and hostname information during install
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to Discord webhooks or other non-standard endpoints during install
file_indicators: package.json with scripts.preinstall referencing node new.js or similar
Presence of new.js or similarly named files in package root
network_indicators: Unusual network activity during npm install, especially to non-standard endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for preinstall scripts that execute external files. Flag packages that access os.networkInterfaces() or os.hostname() in install scripts. Detect outbound HTTPS POST requests to Discord webhooks or other suspicious endpoints during package installation. Use sandboxing to block or alert on network access during install scripts.
